intelligence.enrichment: The Pole Star, or Polaris, is part of the Little Dipper and appears stationary in the North direction, so finding it helps locate North. When the Pole Star is identified, its apparent fixed position marks the North direction; the Big Dipper and Little Dipper patterns help guide the search when they are visible. The learner correctly applies this rule: The Pole Star, or Polaris, is part of the Little Dipper and appears stationary in the North direction, so finding it helps locate North. The largest or easiest dipper pattern must be the North marker, so finding the Big Dipper is the same as finding North.
